## Historical audit: S0222

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_v2_1/results/r2/fixed_h0/H0/selection/commons_194983350/trajectory.jsonl`. Citations below refer to this file. All observations are complete lines, not split observations; the supplied character ranges are included for precision.

| Evidence | Observation and limits |
|---|---|
| Student request, line 1 [0,5616) | The explicit goal was to reconstruct a 342 × 512 indoor photograph with separate meshes and a matching camera, without using the image as a texture. The photograph itself is not visible in this audit. |
| Student response, line 3 [0,11519); execute step 1, line 4 [0,12162) | The student produced and submitted a complete scene program, not an empty patch. Its code describes multiple objects: architecture, shelving, plants, sofa and cushions, table accessories, and three chairs. These names and intended arrangements are not visual verification of the reference or generated scene. |
| Same response and execution | Materials are represented by colors, global roughness and sheen; ceiling mottling is modeled with small colored geometry rather than an image texture. Chair backs, legs, sofa parts and table supports are positioned as separate primitives; their actual connections are unverified. Pillow rotations and chair-back orientations encode intended poses, also unverified. |
| Same response and execution | A camera, three area lights, Cycles settings and 48 samples were specified. Whether framing, illumination, occlusion or rendering matched the photograph is unknown. The large number of generated primitives is a possible performance concern, not an established timeout diagnosis. |
| Student session, line 2 [0,2862); execution result, line 5 [0,1081) | One observable student CLI turn had no tool calls; the runner then attempted one build. Blender timed out after approximately 464 seconds, with empty stdout/stderr and no image. No render inspection, correction, successful build, or final `DONE` is visible. |

**Outcome:** A technical interruption prevented visible validation. The trace does not establish formal success, partial visual correctness, or an algorithmic failure; it also does not establish which build or render stage consumed the time.

**Teacher input and exploration:** No teacher message, detection, diagnosis, proposed update, or adoption is present. The student independently authored one candidate, but no iterative exploration or comparison is visible. The initial session's successful exit concerns generation of the program, not successful scene execution.

**Lessons and uncertainty:** Transferably, a runnable-looking scene specification still requires an actual build and image-based inspection; a timeout alone does not identify its cause. Task-specific hypotheses include whether the dense ceiling, foliage and tuft primitives contributed to runtime, and whether the chosen camera and separate furniture parts would match or connect correctly. None can be resolved from this trace without execution or visual evidence.
